sentences.en: We live in a world in which we tiptoe along a thin line between free will and selfishness, between self-determination and narcissism, between empathy and righteousness.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个世界里，在自由意志与自私之间、在自我决定与自恋之间、在同理心与正义感之间，我们如履薄冰。

sentences.en: Underpinning everything are these crucial questions.
sentences.zh: 支撑这一切的是这些至关重要的问题。

sentences.en: Who am I as an individual?
sentences.zh: 作为一个个体，我是谁？

sentences.en: And who am I as a member of a group and society?
sentences.zh: 作为一个群体和社会的一员，我又是谁？

sentences.en: When did we begin to be as selfish as we are today?
sentences.zh: 我们是从什么时候开始变得像今天这样自私的？

sentences.en: At what point did we expect to have the right to determine our own lives?
sentences.zh: 我们是在什么时候开始认为自己有权决定自己的人生的？

sentences.en: When did we think it was our right to take what we wanted?
sentences.zh: 我们是在什么时候认为索取自己想要的东西是我们的权利的？

sentences.en: Where did this us, you, me, or our collective behavior all come from?
sentences.zh: 这种“我们”、“你们”、“我”，或者说我们的集体行为，究竟是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: And when did we first ask the question, how can I be free?
sentences.zh: 我们又是从什么时候开始第一次提出“我该如何获得自由”这个问题的？

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland, these are questions that I imagine you ask yourself all the time.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·霍兰德，我想这些问题你一定经常问自己。

sentences.en: Every day.
sentences.zh: 每天都在问。

sentences.en: I leap out of bed asking those questions.
sentences.zh: 我从床上跳起来时就在问这些问题。

sentences.en: They're the questions posed in a preface to a wonderful new book, which we'll come to in just a second.
sentences.zh: 这些问题是一本精彩新书的序言中提出的，我们马上就会谈到它。

sentences.en: But people often say, don't they, that we live in an age of unparalleled narcissism.
sentences.zh: 但人们常说，我们生活在一个前所未有的自恋时代，不是吗？

sentences.en: And people often like to trace this back to the ideals of philosophers and writers and people who argued about the self
sentences.zh: 人们常喜欢把这追溯到那些哲学家、作家以及探讨自我的人们的思想，

sentences.en: and the individual and the kind of romantic ideal of the poet in his garret or staring out over a mountain.
sentences.zh: 探讨个体，以及那种阁楼里的诗人或凝视山峦的诗人的浪漫理想。

sentences.en: I mean, this is very much, not only is it your kind of territory, because you love Lord
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅非常符合你的领域，因为你热爱拜伦勋爵，

sentences.en: Byron, who you believe to have been a vampire, but also, but also, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你认为他是个吸血鬼，而且，而且，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, that's very much doing what you want, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常符合“随心所欲”的定义，不是吗？

sentences.en: You are very much this sort of person, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你本人就是这种人，对吧？

sentences.en: I see you as a rugged individual staring out over great mountain ranges, contemplating the...
sentences.zh: 在我眼中，你就像是一个坚毅的个体，凝视着连绵的山脉，沉思着……

sentences.en: That is so kind.
sentences.zh: 你真是太客气了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pejoratively.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是贬义的。

sentences.en: So that's poor behavior by your reckoning.
sentences.zh: 所以按照你的看法，那是糟糕的行为。

sentences.en: Well, I'm Samuel Johnson kicking a stone.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我就是那个踢石头的塞缪尔·约翰逊。

sentences.en: You are.
sentences.zh: 你确实是。

sentences.en: Famously, he kicked a stone and refuted Bishop Barclay's theory of immaterialism.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，他踢了一块石头，以此反驳了巴克莱主教的非物质论。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Byron, but of course, actually, I mean, this is very German behavior.
sentences.zh: 你提到了拜伦，但当然，实际上，我的意思是，这非常具有德国人的行为特征。

sentences.en: It is German.
sentences.zh: 确实很德国。

sentences.en: Because the idea of romanticism, the very word romantic in the way that we use it today,
sentences.zh: 因为浪漫主义这个概念，也就是我们今天所使用的“浪漫”这个词，

sentences.en: originates with a group of German philosophers in the university town of Jena, basically in the
sentences.zh: 起源于18世纪90年代，在耶拿这座大学城里的一群德国哲学家。

sentences.en: And it's the argument of my dear friend, Andrea Wolf, who award-winning historian, and despite being German, writes brilliant, brilliant English.
sentences.zh: 这也是我亲爱的朋友安德烈亚·沃尔夫的论点，她是一位获奖历史学家，尽管是德国人，却写出了极其精彩的英文。

sentences.en: Despite being German.
sentences.zh: 尽管是德国人。

sentences.en: Tom, what an introduction.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这介绍真是绝了。

sentences.en: And her latest book is Magnificent Rebels, The First Romantics and the Invention of the Self.
sentences.zh: 她最新的书是《伟大的叛逆者：第一批浪漫主义者与自我的发明》（Magnificent Rebels, The First Romantics and the Invention of the Self）。

sentences.en: And Andrea, when you told me about this, must have been three, four years ago that you were planning
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚，当你三四年前告诉我这件事时，说你正计划

sentences.en: to write a book about a bunch of philosophers in the university town of Jena, I thought that was a brave choice.
sentences.zh: 写一本关于耶拿大学城里一群哲学家的书，我觉得这是一个勇敢的选择。

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, I mean, Dominic, as a kind of John Bull figure, what is your attitude towards German idealist philosophers?
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，我的意思是，多米尼克，作为一个典型的“约翰牛”式人物，你对德国唯心主义哲学家持什么态度？

sentences.en: Do you read them regularly?
sentences.zh: 你经常读他们的书吗？

sentences.en: Are you a favorite of them?
sentences.zh: 你是他们的拥趸吗？

sentences.en: Do you curl up with shelling of an evening?
sentences.zh: 你会蜷在沙发上读谢林的著作吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, when I'm on the train on the way to Molyneux on a Saturday, Tom, I've often got a volume of Fichte with me, reading a bit of Hegel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，当我在周六乘火车去莫利纽克斯球场时，我经常随身带着一卷费希特，读读黑格尔。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: No, I mean, I think what is absolutely fascinating, Tom, is that this is a world so unknown to English-speaking readers.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，汤姆，我认为最令人着迷的是，对于讲英语的读者来说，这是一个完全未知的世界。

sentences.en: So in other words, we're in 18th century Germany.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们现在身处18世纪的德国。

sentences.en: So Germany has not been unified yet.
sentences.zh: 当时德国尚未统一。

sentences.en: We are, as you say, in the era of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们处于法国大革命时期。

sentences.en: And we are talking about one of the, you know, the most advanced, most sort of civilised, most enlightened, as it were, parts of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是欧洲最先进、最文明、最开明的地区之一。

sentences.en: And all these people who, for many years, actually, in Britain, were seen as absolute paragons and models.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些人，多年来在英国实际上被视为绝对的典范和楷模。

sentences.en: Well, and direct influences on the Romantic movement here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且对这里的浪漫主义运动有直接影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, and have since disappeared, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 是的，但后来他们消失了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think partly because of the world wars, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是由于世界大战，汤姆。

sentences.en: They've sort of been airbrushed out.
sentences.zh: 他们被某种程度上抹去了。

sentences.en: But anyway, tell me about Coleridge.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，跟我说说柯勒律治吧。

sentences.en: Well, so Coleridge goes to study there and basically plagiarises vast chunks of philosophy from Schelling, in particular, this philosopher.
sentences.zh: 好的，柯勒律治去那里学习，基本上抄袭了谢林这位哲学家的大量哲学思想。

sentences.en: And that has a huge influence on English
sentences.zh: 这对英国

sentences.en: Romanticism.
sentences.zh: 浪漫主义产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So the English Romantics, the French Romantics, American Romantics, all absolutely in debt to this.
sentences.zh: 所以英国浪漫主义者、法国浪漫主义者、美国浪漫主义者，都完全受惠于此。

sentences.en: And Andrea, in your introduction, you say, I mean, you express the significance of this
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚，在你的引言中，你表达了这

sentences.en: decade, the 1790s in Jena, in very, very kind of vaunting terms, a mere blink in time, yet one of the most important decades for the shaping of the modern mind.
sentences.zh: 十年，即1790年代的耶拿，其意义非常重大，这仅仅是历史长河中的一瞬，却是塑造现代思想最重要的十年之一。

sentences.en: And it has to be said that you conclusively, I think, make that case.
sentences.zh: 而且必须说，我认为你令人信服地证明了这一点。

sentences.en: And not only do you make that case, but you make it in an incredibly entertaining style.
sentences.zh: 你不仅证明了这一点，而且是以一种极其引人入胜的风格写出来的。

sentences.en: Because although, you know, the philosophy is incredibly important, as you demonstrate, I mean, they are, they're such a bunch, they're endlessly marrying with each
sentences.zh: 因为虽然哲学非常重要，正如你所展示的那样，他们是一群人，他们无休止地与彼此

sentences.en: other, falling out of each other's beds, having spats.
sentences.zh: 结婚、从对方的床上爬起来、发生争吵。

sentences.en: I mean, you've written it almost as a kind of soap opera, verging at points into a sitcom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你把它写得几乎像是一部肥皂剧，有时甚至接近情景喜剧。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, you know, when if the thing is, if you write about philosophy, you need to kind of lighten it up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，如果你写哲学，你需要让它变得轻松一点。

sentences.en: And, and I, and I also think the problem is we see philosophy or philosophers through their works, but obviously, they were people.
sentences.zh: 而且，我也认为问题在于我们通过作品来看待哲学或哲学家，但显然，他们也是人。

sentences.en: And their philosophy was a philosophy of the self.
sentences.zh: 他们的哲学是一种关于自我的哲学。

sentences.en: So they kind of use their own lives as a platform to try this all out.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把自己的生活当作试验场来尝试这一切。

sentences.en: So they became quite egotistical also.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也变得相当自负。

sentences.en: So it's, it's a book about big, big ideas about the beginning of the modern self.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一本关于宏大思想、关于现代自我起源的书。

sentences.en: But it is also a soap opera with lots of sex and rock and roll and fun.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一部充满性、摇滚乐和乐趣的肥皂剧。

sentences.en: And, you know, because, because we have thousands and thousands of letters, and these are all poets, so they write really well and really gossipy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为我们有成千上万封信件，而且他们都是诗人，所以他们写得非常好，而且非常八卦。

sentences.en: So because we have these letters, you can actually you can enter the rooms with them, you can enter the bedroom with them.
sentences.zh: 因为有这些信件，你可以真正进入他们的房间，进入他们的卧室。

sentences.en: I mean, one of them wrote an erotic autobiographical novel, where he basically invites the readers to watch him and his lover make love in quite explicit erotic detail.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一个人写了一部色情自传体小说，他基本上邀请读者观看他和他的爱人做爱，细节非常露骨。

sentences.en: So, so they're, they're philosophers, but they're also very flawed human beings.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们是哲学家，但也是非常有缺陷的人类。

sentences.en: Well, you, you, you quote Navalis, who is the kind of the prototype of the doomed romantic poet,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你引用了诺瓦利斯，他是那种注定失败的浪漫主义诗人的原型，

sentences.en: great poet who dies young, age of 29, I think, so the prototype for Keats and Shelley and all that
sentences.zh: 伟大的诗人，英年早逝，我想是29岁，所以他是济慈和雪莱等人的原型，

sentences.en: stuff, which he frames as lewdness raged from morning into the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为“淫欲从早晨一直狂乱到下午”。

sentences.en: So I know, but then you, if you go on, there's one where the, the lewd fantasy in the morning leads to an explosion in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我知道，但如果你继续读下去，还有一段是说早晨的淫乱幻想导致了下午的爆发。

sentences.en: Oh my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, so, so, so this is very much a collection of people who are not just doing philosophy, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅仅是一群人在做哲学研究。

sentences.en: So let's put them, Andrea, in place and in time.
sentences.zh: 那么安德烈亚，让我们把他们放在特定的时间和地点。

sentences.en: So we are at the end of the 18th century, and we are in a place called Jena.
sentences.zh: 我们处于18世纪末，地点是耶拿。

sentences.en: There was a battle of Jena, which we might come to later, but first of all, so where is Jena and why should we be interested in it?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了耶拿战役，我们以后可能会谈到，但首先，耶拿在哪里？为什么我们应该对它感兴趣？

sentences.en: So maybe I should start with Germany, just to explain a little bit where Jena is, because Jena is in Germany.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该从德国开始，解释一下耶拿在哪里，因为耶拿在德国。

sentences.en: So as you said in your introduction, Germany at the end of the 18th century is not a unified nation.
sentences.zh: 正如你在引言中所说，18世纪末的德国不是一个统一的国家。

sentences.en: It's a patchwork of 1500 states, ranging from tiny principalities to big, you know, mighty states like Prussia and Austria.
sentences.zh: 它是一个由1500个邦国组成的拼凑体，从微小的公国到普鲁士和奥地利这样强大的国家。

sentences.en: And, and Jena is in the duchy of Saxe-Weimar, which is in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 耶拿位于萨克森-魏玛公国，就在中间。

sentences.en: But the unintended advantage of this fragmentation is that
sentences.zh: 但这种碎片化的意外优势在于，

sentences.en: censorship is basically very difficult to enforce in these little states, because every state has a different set of rules.
sentences.zh: 审查制度在这些小邦国里基本上很难执行，因为每个邦国都有不同的规则。

sentences.en: So very unlike century ruled countries like England or France, and France,
sentences.zh: 所以这与英国或法国这种中央集权国家非常不同，

sentences.en: England, Spain have also big, you know, they're big global monarchies, powerful monarchies with a global reach through their colonies.
sentences.zh: 英国、西班牙也是全球性的大君主国，通过殖民地拥有全球影响力。

sentences.en: And in Germany, everything is inward looking and splintered.
sentences.zh: 而在德国，一切都是向内看且分裂的。

sentences.en: So the German imagination really has to, is fed by words and by, by, by, by books, and Germans are fanatical readers.
sentences.zh: 所以德国人的想象力确实是由文字和书籍滋养的，德国人是狂热的读者。

sentences.en: So the literacy rates in Germany are much higher than elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以德国的识字率远高于其他地方。

sentences.en: So Saxony and Prussia actually lead the world at the end of the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 萨克森和普鲁士在18世纪末实际上处于世界领先地位。

sentences.en: They're more universities.
sentences.zh: 那里有更多的大学。

sentences.en: I was, I mean, I was really startled to read in your, and a little bit embarrassed on behalf of
sentences.zh: 我读到你的书时真的很吃惊，而且我不得不说，我代表英国感到有点尴尬，

sentences.en: England, I'm afraid to say, that the German book trade in was, was four to five times larger than
sentences.zh: 德国的图书贸易规模是英国的四到五倍，

sentences.en: that in England, which isn't at all the impression that one would get from, you know, reading about
sentences.zh: 这与人们从阅读伦敦格拉布街（Grub Street）之类的文章中得到的印象完全不同。

sentences.en: Grub Street in London or something.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, and everybody read in Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且在德国，每个人都读书。

sentences.en: I mean, we can, you can not underestimate how many people read in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你无法低估德国读书人的数量。

sentences.en: So, and you have 50 universities compared to two universities in England.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有50所大学，而英国只有两所。

sentences.en: So ideas and arguments traveled quite easily through the German states.
sentences.zh: 因此，思想和争论在德国各邦之间传播得非常容易。

sentences.en: But then the question is why
sentences.zh: 但问题是为什么是

sentences.en: Jena?
sentences.zh: 耶拿？

sentences.en: So Jena is this small town, four and a half thousand inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 耶拿是一个小镇，有四千五百名居民。

sentences.en: It's a university town, it's tiny.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大学城，非常小。

sentences.en: So it takes like less than 10 minutes to cross.
sentences.zh: 穿过它只需要不到10分钟。

sentences.en: It's headed by a pretty enlightened ruler who encourages a certain degree of openness and, and frankness.
sentences.zh: 它由一位相当开明的统治者领导，鼓励一定程度的开放和坦率。

sentences.en: And, but the real reason why there's more freedom in Jena and why it attracts more liberally minded people than anywhere else in
sentences.zh: 但耶拿之所以比德国其他任何地方都有更多的自由，吸引了更多思想自由的人，真正的原因是大学的管理，它曾经属于萨克森，但通过

sentences.en: Germany is the governance of the university through, which once belonged to Saxony, but through
sentences.zh: 复杂的继承法，名义上由四个不同的萨克森公爵控制，没有人真正负责。

sentences.en: complicated inheritance laws, basically nominally kind of controlled by four different Saxon dukes, no one is in charge.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，每个在家乡遇到当局问题的作家、思想家最终都会来到耶拿。

sentences.en: So what happens is every writer, every thinker who has, you know, problems with the authorities in their hometowns ends up in Jena.
sentences.zh: 所以它成为了一个非常短暂的革命思想聚集地。

sentences.en: So it becomes this very transient place of very revolutionary minds.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，一个很好的例子是它太短暂了，

sentences.en: And I mean, it's one, for me, one great example was that it's so transient that
sentences.zh: 以至于在耶拿时期，耶拿出生的小孩中有惊人的25%，即四分之一是私生子。

sentences.en: you have a staggering amount of 25%, a quarter of all children born in Jena at the time of the Jena set are born out of wedlock.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有很多性行为。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of sex going on there.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 而且它是一个非常小、非常亲密的地方，不是吗？

sentences.en: And, and it's a very kind of small, intimate place, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 你在书中反复提到，这是一个太小而无法藏住八卦的地方。

sentences.en: And you say again and again throughout the book that it's a place that's too small for gossip.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，当人们开始与某人发生关系或在背后议论他人时，总会传到当事人耳中。

sentences.en: So essentially, when people start sleeping with one another or bitching about them behind their backs, it always gets back to them.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常适合肥皂剧的漩涡和戏剧性。

sentences.en: And so it's ideally suited to the swirl and drama of soap opera.

sentences.zh: 这就是他们的知识意图。

sentences.zh: 奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔也是一位杰出的翻译家，他和妻子一起翻译了16部莎士比亚剧作，这是第一部德语诗体译本，
zh_words: 奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔

sentences.en: which to this day is the standard edition.
sentences.zh: 至今仍是标准版本。

sentences.en: And amazingly, his published lectures on Shakespeare, which were very much informed by his discussion with his wife, then resurrected Shakespeare in England, believe it or not.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，他出版的关于莎士比亚的讲座，很大程度上得益于与妻子的讨论，信不信由你，这让莎士比亚在英国复活了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Germany.
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢谢你，德国。

sentences.en: William Wordsworth said that a German critic taught us correctly, how to think correctly about Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 威廉·华兹华斯说，一位德国评论家正确地教导了我们如何正确地思考莎士比亚。

sentences.en: So they are actually quite an important bunch of people.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实是一群非常重要的人。

sentences.en: Because that's the joke, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这就是笑话所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: That the German version is very good and the English translation of it isn't bad as well.
sentences.zh: 德语版本非常好，而它的英语翻译也不错。

sentences.en: Well, I have to say, I mean, I really like, I mean, I live in England and I've lived here for almost 30 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我必须说，我真的很喜欢，我在英国住了快30年了。

sentences.en: I always read English stuff.
sentences.zh: 我总是读英语的东西。

sentences.en: But German Shakespeare performances are pretty good.
sentences.zh: 但德国的莎士比亚演出相当不错。

sentences.en: I think I almost prefer them to the English ones.
sentences.zh: 我想我几乎更喜欢德国版的。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm hanging myself out of the window.
sentences.zh: 噢，我这是在自找麻烦。

sentences.en: So, Andrea, you mentioned Schlegel's wife, who is the co-translator on this.
sentences.zh: 那么，安德烈亚，你提到了施莱格尔的妻子，她是这部作品的合译者。

sentences.en: And she is an extraordinary woman.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非凡的女性。

sentences.en: And in a way, she seems to be the beating heart of the soap opera, the sitcom, however you want to frame it.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，她似乎是这场肥皂剧、情景喜剧——无论你怎么称呼它——的核心。

sentences.en: I mean, she's a remarkable figure, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是个了不起的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: So just tell me about her.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲她吧。

sentences.en: So let me introduce her properly with all her names.
sentences.zh: 让我用她所有的名字正式介绍她。

sentences.en: She is Karoline Michaelis Böhmer Schlegel Schelling.
sentences.zh: 她是卡罗琳·米夏埃利斯·伯默尔·施莱格尔·谢林。
zh_words: 埃利斯·伯默尔·施莱格尔·谢林

sentences.en: So she carries the name of her father and her three husbands.
sentences.zh: 她冠有她父亲和三任丈夫的姓氏。

sentences.en: And she is, as you said, she's at the heart of this story.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她是这个故事的核心。

sentences.en: She was born in 1763.
sentences.zh: 她出生于1763年。

sentences.en: She was the daughter of a very famous German scholar.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常著名的德国学者的女儿。

sentences.en: She was raised on a diet on literature, poetry and politics.
sentences.zh: 她在文学、诗歌和政治的熏陶下长大。

sentences.en: She was beautiful, educated, fiercely independently minded.
sentences.zh: 她美丽、受过良好教育，且思想极其独立。

sentences.en: She married young, was a widow by the age of 24, then hung out with the German revolutionaries,
sentences.zh: 她早早结婚，24岁就成了寡妇，随后又与德国革命者混在一起，

sentences.en: was then imprisoned by the Prussians for being a sympathizer with the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 后来因为同情法国大革命而被普鲁士人关进了监狱。

sentences.en: And then not only that, in prison, she discovered that she was pregnant after a one night stand with an 18-year-old French soldier.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，她在狱中发现自己怀孕了，那是她与一名18岁的法国士兵一夜情的结果。

sentences.en: So quite something at a time when it was scandalous behavior, if you were just on your own in a room with a man.
sentences.zh: 在那个如果一个女人独自和男人待在一个房间里都会被视为丑闻的时代，这简直太惊世骇俗了。

sentences.en: Then after her imprisonment, she kind of zigzagged through Germany, was treated as an outcaSt.
sentences.zh: 出狱后，她在德国四处漂泊，被视为社会弃儿。

sentences.en: And then August Wilhelm Schlegel came along.
sentences.zh: 然后，奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔出现了。
zh_words: 奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔

sentences.en: I mean, men just fell for her.
sentences.zh: 我是说，男人们都为她倾倒。

sentences.en: So he was in love with her.
sentences.zh: 他爱上了她。

sentences.en: He married her, gave her a new name.
sentences.zh: 他娶了她，给了她一个新的名字。

sentences.en: And with that, a new beginning and took her to Jena in 1796, where she really became the heart of the Jena set and not the muse.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一个全新的开始，1796年他带她去了耶拿，在那里她真正成为了“耶拿圈”的核心，而不仅仅是缪斯。

sentences.en: She's not just the muse.
sentences.zh: 她不仅仅是缪斯。

sentences.en: She's much, much more important.
sentences.zh: 她要重要得多，重要得多。

sentences.en: Participant.
sentences.zh: 她是参与者。

sentences.en: Yeah, so she does the kind of more traditional thing where she creates the physical space for them, where they all meet and work together and party.
sentences.zh: 没错，她做了那种更传统的事情，为他们创造了物理空间，让他们聚在一起工作和聚会。

sentences.en: But she's also a razor-sharp critic who dissects poetry and plays and essays with deep, deep knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但她同时也是一位极其敏锐的评论家，能以深厚的学识剖析诗歌、戏剧和散文。

sentences.en: And her husband and her friends begin to rely on her literary and analytical mind.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫和朋友们开始依赖她的文学和分析头脑。

sentences.en: She is the editor of the Athenaeum.
sentences.zh: 她是《雅典娜神殿》杂志的编辑。

sentences.en: So she takes the role of the editor.
sentences.zh: 她承担了编辑的角色。

sentences.en: She writes reviews under her husband's name.
sentences.zh: 她以丈夫的名义撰写评论。

sentences.en: I mean, many, many, many.
sentences.zh: 我是说，写了很多很多篇。

sentences.en: And she translates together with her husband the 16 Shakespeare plays, which, of course, was never acknowledged.
sentences.zh: 她还与丈夫一起翻译了16部莎士比亚戏剧，当然，这些贡献从未得到承认。

sentences.en: So her name is not on any of these books.
sentences.zh: 所以这些书上都没有她的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just wanted to ask about that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我正想问这个。

sentences.en: So what are the possibilities for a highly educated, highly intelligent woman in Jena at the end of the 18th century?
sentences.zh: 那么，18世纪末在耶拿，一位受过高等教育、极其聪明的女性有什么出路呢？

sentences.en: Does she have to do it all through, sort of, as it were, using her husband as a vehicle?
sentences.zh: 她是否必须通过某种方式，比如利用她的丈夫作为媒介来完成这一切？

sentences.en: I mean, what do people think of such an articulate, emboldened woman?
sentences.zh: 人们是怎么看待这样一位口才好、胆识过人的女性的？

sentences.en: So it was difficult.
sentences.zh: 这很困难。

sentences.en: So most women published either anonymously or under that name of their husbands.
sentences.zh: 大多数女性要么匿名发表作品，要么用丈夫的名字发表。

sentences.en: There were a few who did not.
sentences.zh: 也有少数人没有这样做。

sentences.en: But I think Karolina chose purposefully not to put her name on there because she was really famous in German for being this revolutionary whore.
sentences.zh: 但我认为卡罗琳是有意选择不署名的，因为她在德国确实以“革命荡妇”而闻名。

sentences.en: So it would have been not a good, you know, strategy financially to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以从经济策略上来说，那样做并不明智。

sentences.en: But it, I mean, Schiller, for example, he had another magazine and he published quite a lot of female writers, but all of them anonymously.
sentences.zh: 不过，席勒也有另一本杂志，他发表了不少女性作家的作品，但全都是匿名的。

sentences.en: So most women would not put their name on there.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数女性不会在上面署名。

sentences.en: It changed.
sentences.zh: 后来情况变了。

sentences.en: I mean, it changes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，确实变了。

sentences.en: There are a few who later do this.
sentences.zh: 后来有少数人开始这么做了。

sentences.en: But it is, I mean, if there is a place in Germany, then it was Jena that you could do that.
sentences.zh: 但如果说德国有什么地方能做到这一点，那一定就是耶拿。

sentences.en: So Friedrich Schlegel, for example, his lover is the divorced Dorothea Veidt.
sentences.zh: 比如弗里德里希·施莱格尔，他的情人是离过婚的多萝西娅·法伊特。

sentences.en: And she's a writer and she writes a novel, but she also publishes it under the name of her husband.
sentences.zh: 她也是一位作家，写了一部小说，但也是以她丈夫的名义出版的。

sentences.en: It's a very, very common thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是非常非常普遍的做法。

sentences.en: So Friedrich Schlegel, younger brother of August Wilhelm Schlegel.
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·施莱格尔是奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔的弟弟。
zh_words: 奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔

sentences.en: And this is why the sitcom element starts to come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是情景喜剧元素开始介入的地方。

sentences.en: So inevitably he meets Karolina and he, I mean, he quite fancies her, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，他遇到了卡罗琳，而且他，我是说，他挺喜欢她的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's younger.
sentences.zh: 他比较年轻。

sentences.en: I mean, she really has a thing for younger men.
sentences.zh: 她确实对年轻男性情有独钟。

sentences.en: There's a moment when she has an affair with the 12-year-old younger Friedrich Schelling.
sentences.zh: 有一次她和比她小12岁的弗里德里希·谢林发生了婚外情。

sentences.en: I'm sorry that everybody's called Friedrich and then Sch at the end.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，每个人都叫弗里德里希，而且姓氏结尾都是Sch。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's really confusing.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人困惑。

sentences.en: Two Schlegels.
sentences.zh: 两个施莱格尔。

sentences.en: No, three Schlegels.
sentences.zh: 不，三个施莱格尔。

sentences.en: And then there's Friedrich Schiller and a Schelling.
sentences.zh: 还有弗里德里希·席勒和一个谢林。

sentences.en: Schiller and a Schelling.
sentences.zh: 席勒和谢林。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's very complicated.
sentences.zh: 这太复杂了。

sentences.en: So Friedrich Schlegel falls in love with Karolina, but then kind of steps back because his brother had first fallen in love with her.
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·施莱格尔爱上了卡罗琳，但后来退缩了，因为他哥哥先爱上了她。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it's all these kind of siblings falling in love with, you know, the same person and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这种兄弟姐妹爱上同一个人之类的戏码。

sentences.en: There seems to be a running theme.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个贯穿始终的主题。

sentences.en: Well, I would say, I mean, so the Schlegel brothers and Karolina and Dorothea Feit, who's the lover of Friedrich Schlegel, they all live together in one house.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想说的是，施莱格尔兄弟、卡罗琳，还有弗里德里希·施莱格尔的情人多萝西娅·法伊特，他们都住在一栋房子里。

sentences.en: And I would really call that the first German commune.
sentences.zh: 我真的会称之为德国第一个公社。

sentences.en: I mean, that's where it all started, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，一切就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because they all, you know, they all live together.
sentences.zh: 因为他们都住在一起。

sentences.en: And Friedrich Schlegel has, he writes these fragments where he says, like, you know, how could anyone have anything against like a marriage, a cadre?
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·施莱格尔写过一些片段，他说，怎么会有人反对这种婚姻形式呢？

sentences.en: So it's a very, I mean, I've not found any letters that indicate that they had like a foursome or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我没发现任何信件表明他们有过四人行之类的行为。

sentences.en: But you have August Wilhelm and Karolina being married in their open marriage.
sentences.zh: 但奥古斯特·威廉和卡罗琳确实维持着开放式婚姻。

sentences.en: And then a few years in, she falls in love with the 12 year old, 12 year younger Friedrich Schelling.
sentences.zh: 几年后，她爱上了比她小12岁的弗里德里希·谢林。

sentences.en: I was going to say, he's not 12 years old.
sentences.zh: 我刚才想说，他不是12岁。

sentences.en: That would be very precocious.
sentences.zh: 那也太早熟了。

sentences.en: He was 12 years younger.
sentences.zh: 他是小12岁。

sentences.en: Well, you know, Novalis fell in love with the 12 year old.
sentences.zh: 嗯，诺瓦利斯爱上了一个12岁的女孩。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to Novalis in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿再谈诺瓦利斯。

sentences.en: And then, and then August Wilhelm doesn't really mind because he has lovers also.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯特·威廉并不介意，因为他自己也有情人。

sentences.en: So it's all, you know, very open and very casual.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都很开放，很随意。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's just come to Novalis, who is the archetype of the Romantic poet, because he dies young.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈诺瓦利斯，他是浪漫主义诗人的原型，因为他英年早逝。

sentences.en: He's a friend of Friedrich Schlegel.
sentences.zh: 他是弗里德里希·施莱格尔的朋友。

sentences.en: In fact, he dies, Friedrich Schlegel is by his bedside.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他去世时，弗里德里希·施莱格尔就在床边。

sentences.en: And he becomes the archetype of the, you know, the beautiful angel, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他成了那种“美丽天使”的原型，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But actually, in some ways, he's a more conventional figure than any of these kind of philosophers hanging out in their commune, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在某些方面，他比那些在公社里闲逛的哲学家们更传统，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's, he's basically running a load of mines.
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上是在经营一堆矿山。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, he's, he's from, he's, he's the only one who's an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是唯一一个贵族。

sentences.en: So he comes from a privileged background, but the family doesn't have a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 他出身优越，但家里并没有多少钱。

sentences.en: They just have basically their lineage.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上只有家世。

sentences.en: And so he runs the mines, together with his father, the salt mines.
sentences.zh: 所以他和父亲一起经营矿山，盐矿。

sentences.en: So he is the only one actually who has a proper job compared to the others.
sentences.zh: 所以他是唯一一个与其他人相比有正经工作的人。

sentences.en: And he, so he studies in, in Jena and then in Leipzig, where he meets Friedrich Schlegel, they become like best friends.
sentences.zh: 他在耶拿和莱比锡学习，在那里遇到了弗里德里希·施莱格尔，他们成了最好的朋友。

sentences.en: And then Novalis is pretty obsessed with Fichte's philosophy of the self.
sentences.zh: 诺瓦利斯非常痴迷于费希特的自我哲学。

sentences.en: Yes, because you say that he wanted to make his body disappear and become spirit alone.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为你说过他想让自己的身体消失，只留下精神。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's, I mean, what exactly does he mean by that?
sentences.zh: 那他到底是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: What's, no one really knows, but he wants to basically transcend the kind of boundaries between, you know, the body and the mind.
sentences.zh: 没人真正知道，但他基本上是想超越身体和心灵之间的界限。

sentences.en: Or the lewdness.
sentences.zh: 或者说超越那种肉欲。

sentences.en: But, but, but what is interesting is, so he falls in love with the 12 year old Sophie von Kuhn, which kind of makes for slightly uncomfortable reading now.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他爱上了12岁的苏菲·冯·库恩，这在今天读起来让人感到有些不适。

sentences.en: And then she dies after some terrible, you know, surgery when she's 15.
sentences.zh: 她在15岁时因为一次可怕的手术去世了。

sentences.en: And Novalis then takes Fichte's philosophy and gives it his very kind of own twist because he says, well, if the ich,
sentences.zh: 诺瓦利斯随后采用了费希特的哲学，并赋予了它自己独特的解读，因为他说，如果“自我”能创造外部世界并控制一切，

sentences.en: if the self can basically create the external world and can control everything, I'm going to kill myself because I want to be reunited with Sophie.
sentences.zh: 那么我要自杀，因为我想与苏菲重聚。

sentences.en: But I'm not going to do it with a gun or rope.
sentences.zh: 但我不会用枪或绳子。

sentences.en: I'm going to do it with sheer willpower just in, he believes that, you know, if our mind can move our body, surely, you know,
sentences.zh: 我要用纯粹的意志力，他相信如果我们的思想能移动身体，那么，

sentences.en: our mind should be able to like regrow an amputated arm and kill us.
sentences.zh: 我们的思想也应该能让断掉的手臂重新长出来，或者杀死我们自己。

sentences.en: So he is, it's a little bit bonkers, but it leads him to write, I think, some of the most exquisite poetry that the young romantics have produced, which is hymns to the night.
sentences.zh: 这有点疯狂，但它促使他写出了我认为是年轻浪漫主义者创作的最精致的诗歌，即《夜颂》。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's a, it's a cycle of six poems and it's just absolutely stunning.
sentences.zh: 那是一组六首诗，简直令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And he plays with, with darkness and with death in a completely new way.
sentences.zh: 他以一种全新的方式处理黑暗与死亡。

sentences.en: So darkness becomes something positive, you know, before darkness has always been something kind of scary, but he,
sentences.zh: 黑暗变成了一种积极的东西，要知道，以前黑暗总是某种可怕的东西，但他，

sentences.en: and I think he uses also his experiences from the minds because in the minds you go into the bowels of the earth.
sentences.zh: 我想他也利用了他在矿山的经历，因为在矿井里，你会深入地球的腹地。

sentences.en: And so the darkness becomes this metaphor for going into you, into yourself, which, you know, is to this day a metaphor we use for us.
sentences.zh: 所以黑暗成为了深入内心的一种隐喻，直到今天我们仍在使用这个隐喻。

sentences.en: But, but also he, I mean, it's interesting because he, presumably in the minds, I mean, he's, he's seeing wheels turn and all this kind of stuff, but he has this,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他在矿井里肯定看到了轮子转动之类的东西，但他有一种抱怨，

sentences.en: this complaint that nature basically by enlightenment philosophy has been reduced to a monotonous machine,
sentences.zh: 即自然被启蒙哲学简化成了一台单调的机器，

sentences.en: turning the eternally creative music of the universe into the monotonous clatter of a gigantic mill wheel.
sentences.zh: 将宇宙永恒的创造性音乐变成了巨大磨坊轮单调的咔哒声。

sentences.en: And that is a theme that is so important to the romantics, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这对于浪漫主义者来说是一个非常重要的主题，不是吗？

sentences.en: This rejection of the enlightenment idea that everything is just cogs and wheels turning.
sentences.zh: 拒绝启蒙运动那种认为一切都只是齿轮和轮子转动的观点。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So they basically turn against these kind of mechanical models of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上反对这种机械的世界观。

sentences.en: So you have, for example, Descartes, who says, who declares all animals to be machines.
sentences.zh: 比如笛卡尔，他宣称所有动物都是机器。

sentences.en: So they, and then you have, you obviously you have an increasing productivity, you have the enlightenment, you have steam engines,
sentences.zh: 然后生产力不断提高，有了启蒙运动，有了蒸汽机，

sentences.en: you have scientists who kind of peer through microscopes to understand the minutia of life, you have them looking into the heavens to understand our, our place in the universe,
sentences.zh: 科学家们透过显微镜观察生命的细节，仰望星空以了解我们在宇宙中的位置，

sentences.en: you have physicians inoculating against smallpox.
sentences.zh: 医生们接种天花疫苗。

sentences.en: So the world becomes this, you know, measurable, repeatable, classifiable kind of machine.
sentences.zh: 世界变成了一台可测量、可重复、可分类的机器。

sentences.en: And that's what the romantics turn againSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是浪漫主义者所反对的。

sentences.en: They don't turn against reason, but what they want is they want to poeticize the sciences.
sentences.zh: 他们并不反对理性，但他们想要的是将科学诗意化。

sentences.en: They want to stop this, what they say, this mill wheel,
sentences.zh: 他们想停止这种他们所说的“磨坊轮”，

sentences.en: which kind of grounds itself to dust because they believe that the enlightenment has stripped the reality of the awe and wonder for nature.
sentences.zh: 它将自身磨成尘埃，因为他们认为启蒙运动剥夺了现实中对自然的敬畏和惊叹。

sentences.en: So what they really believe is that the external world has become something that has to be observed from a so-called objective perspective.
sentences.zh: 他们真正相信的是，外部世界已经变成了一种必须从所谓的客观视角去观察的对象。

sentences.en: And they say, and this is where Friedrich Schelling comes in with his philosophy, they basically say the self and nature is one.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这就是弗里德里希·谢林提出他的哲学的地方，他们基本上说自我和自然是一体的。

sentences.en: It's a unity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个统一体。

sentences.en: Everything is one big living organism.
sentences.zh: 一切都是一个巨大的生命有机体。

sentences.en: So if we are part of nature, if the system of nature and the system of the mind is the same thing, it means that when we walk through nature, when we, you know, go for, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们是自然的一部分，如果自然的系统和心灵的系统是同一回事，这意味着当我们走进自然，当我们去，

sentences.en: walk through a forest or scramble up a mountain, it's always a journey of self-discovery.
sentences.zh: 穿过森林或爬上山峰时，这总是一次自我发现的旅程。

sentences.en: So this philosophy of oneness, that becomes the heartbeat of romanticism.
sentences.zh: 所以这种“合一”的哲学，成为了浪漫主义的心跳。

sentences.en: That is at the kind of the, the neck at the nexus of everything.
sentences.zh: 这是所有一切的核心。

sentences.en: And that is what then becomes so important for the English romantics and for the American transcendentalists.
sentences.zh: 这后来对英国浪漫主义者和美国超验主义者变得非常重要。

sentences.en: The irony, though, is that, of course, they're talking all the time about unity, but they are incredibly divided among themselves, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，他们一直在谈论统一，但他们内部却极其分裂，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you, you call them the Janus set, but I mean, there's nobody they hate more than one another.
sentences.zh: 你称他们为“耶拿圈”，但他们之间简直恨不得对方死。

sentences.en: Or am I being, am I?
sentences.zh: 还是说我太刻薄了？

sentences.en: Well, imagine this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想象一下。

sentences.en: You have a bunch of rebellious young women and men who live together in a small town and they have declared their self as the supreme ruler of the world.
sentences.zh: 一群叛逆的年轻人住在一个小镇里，他们宣称自己是世界的主宰。

sentences.en: You're kind of bound to end up with inflated egos, self-absorption and fight.
sentences.zh: 你们注定会变得自负、自我沉溺并发生争吵。

sentences.en: And it's exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 事实也正是如此。

sentences.en: They end up in what Dorothea Weid calls a republic of despots.
sentences.zh: 他们最终陷入了多萝西娅·法伊特所说的“暴君共和国”。

sentences.en: That's what they become.
sentences.zh: 他们变成了那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's also, I mean, the arguments that they have are not merely arguments on the page, are they?
sentences.zh: 但他们争论的不仅仅是纸面上的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's a scene in which students are throwing bricks through Fichte's windows because they despise his ideas so much.
sentences.zh: 有一个场景是学生们向费希特的窗户扔砖头，因为他们太鄙视他的思想了。

sentences.en: And Goethe says, you know, this is a very disagreeable way for Fichte to have the existence of a non-ich proven to.
sentences.zh: 歌德说，这对于费希特来说，是一种非常令人不快的方式来证明“非我”的存在。

sentences.en: So these are things that people are actually, I mean, maybe fighting, physically fighting is too strong an expression,
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情是人们真的，我是说，也许说“打架”太强烈了，

sentences.en: but they are prepared to, at least, if not to take up arms, then to take up bricks about.
sentences.zh: 但他们至少准备好了，如果不是拿起武器，那也要拿起砖头。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, in the beginning, they kind of agree, but they're obviously fighting the literary establishment.
sentences.zh: 起初他们意见一致，但他们显然是在与文学建制派作斗争。

sentences.en: And the literary establishment hates them.
sentences.zh: 而文学建制派讨厌他们。

sentences.en: I mean, like, hates them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们简直恨透了这些人。

sentences.en: They write satires about them.
sentences.zh: 他们写讽刺文章来抨击这些人。

sentences.en: They write really, really savage reviews about them.
sentences.zh: 他们写下非常、非常刻薄的评论来攻击他们。

sentences.en: So, but they, it's almost like they're just fired up by this.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们，这简直就像是这些事反而激起了他们的斗志。

sentences.en: They just love it because, and there's a wonderful quote where August Wilhelm Schliegel kind of says, it's like, they hate us great.
sentences.zh: 他们乐在其中，因为——有一句精彩的引语，奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔曾说，大意是，他们恨我们恨得好。
zh_words: 奥古斯特·威廉·施莱格尔

sentences.en: They curse us even better.
sentences.zh: 他们诅咒我们诅咒得更妙。

sentences.en: They, you know, they want, they call us blasphemers, even more fabulous.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道，他们想要，他们称我们为亵渎者，这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: So they quite like the, the fight.
sentences.zh: 所以他们其实挺享受这种争斗的。

sentences.en: But then in the end, they turn against each other.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他们开始反目成仇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It starts to kind of break up, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 一切开始分崩离析了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Victor flounces off.
sentences.zh: 因为维克多愤然离去。

sentences.en: I mean, he basically says, back me or I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他基本上是说，要么支持我，要么我就走人。

sentences.en: And they release the back end.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就放手了。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: It's the beginning of the breakup is really when, when Friedrich Schliegel very stupidly writes a savage or several savage reviews about Schiller's works,
sentences.zh: 真正的决裂始于弗里德里希·施莱格尔非常愚蠢地写了一篇或几篇关于席勒作品的刻薄评论时，

sentences.en: including criticizing Schiller's magazine Hohen for having too many translations in there.
sentences.zh: 其中包括批评席勒的杂志《霍伦》里翻译作品太多。

sentences.en: But his brother himself wrote these, you know, these translations.
sentences.zh: 但他的兄弟本人就写过这些，你知道，这些翻译作品。

sentences.en: So Fichte in the end, Schiller in the end just goes like, oh my gosh, can't deal with these guys anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以费希特最终，席勒最终只是觉得，天哪，我再也无法应付这些人了。

sentences.en: And he basically breaks off all contact.
sentences.zh: 他基本上断绝了所有联系。

sentences.en: And this is, this is really when it starts because Schiller had originally brought them to Yale.
sentences.zh: 而这，这才是真正的开始，因为席勒最初是把他们带到耶拿的。

sentences.en: So this is, and then, and then you have Schiller who calls Caroline Madame Lucifer and Wilhelm von Hombor's wife calls her a snake.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是，然后，然后席勒称卡罗琳为“路西法夫人”，而威廉·冯·洪堡的妻子称她为“毒蛇”。

sentences.en: And it just goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这种事没完没了。

sentences.en: And then women tend to be less keen on Caroline than men.
sentences.zh: 而且女性往往不像男性那样喜欢卡罗琳。

sentences.en: Would it be fair to say?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: That's definitely fair to say.
sentences.zh: 这绝对公平。

sentences.en: And I think that that was because she never, she was never willing to play the kind of demure domestic housewife.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为她从来不愿扮演那种端庄贤淑的家庭主妇角色。

sentences.en: She was, you know, she was always like, I'm going to hang out with a, with a man here.
sentences.zh: 她总是，你知道，她总是说，我要和男人混在一起。

sentences.en: I'm not going to hang out.
sentences.zh: 我才不要待在家里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One of my favourite bits in the whole book was when, and as you say,
sentences.zh: 整本书里我最喜欢的部分之一就是，正如你所说，

sentences.en: they're always kind of flancing out and having bust ups and writing negative reviews of each other in magazines and things.
sentences.zh: 他们总是愤然离场、发生争吵，并在杂志上写文章互相攻击等等。

sentences.en: And Schlegel announces that he's leaving one of them.
sentences.zh: 然后施莱格尔宣布他要离开其中一个人。

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, it was simply too embarrassing to write alongside so many inferior contributors.
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，和这么多低水平的投稿人一起写作实在太尴尬了。

sentences.en: Oh my word, Tom.
sentences.zh: 天哪，汤姆。

sentences.en: So there's something perhaps for you to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许是你需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: What, with my podcast co-presenter?
sentences.zh: 什么，关于我的播客联合主持人吗？

sentences.en: No, I was thinking, I was thinking more of your many media entanglement.
sentences.zh: 不，我在想，我在想你那众多的媒体纠葛。

sentences.en: You're thinking about other media outlets.
sentences.zh: 你在想其他的媒体渠道。

sentences.en: I am thinking about other media outlets.
sentences.zh: 我确实在想其他的媒体渠道。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: But what about, hold on.
sentences.zh: 但是等等，等一下。

sentences.en: What about, what about, what about Schelling when he gets a bad review suggesting to the editors that the only person who could write a review about his own book is himself?
sentences.zh: 那谢林呢？当他收到差评时，他向编辑建议，唯一能为他的书写评论的人只有他自己？

sentences.en: We all think that though, don't we?
sentences.zh: 但我们都这么想，不是吗？

sentences.en: We all think that.
sentences.zh: 我们都这么想。

sentences.en: So Schiller has broken up with the kind of younger set.
sentences.zh: 所以席勒已经和那群年轻人决裂了。

sentences.en: Victor storms off and goes off, has to go off to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 维克多愤然离去，不得不去了柏林。

sentences.en: And then you mentioned Schelling.
sentences.zh: 然后你提到了谢林。

sentences.en: And Schelling ends up married to Carolina.
sentences.zh: 谢林最终和卡罗琳结婚了。

sentences.en: So that presumably also isn't, I mean, it's not hugely helpful to the group harmonies, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这大概也不是，我是说，这对团队和谐没什么帮助，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, no, that is one of the other reasons why it kind of all breaks apart.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，这是导致一切分崩离析的其他原因之一。

sentences.en: But not so much, not because of August Wilhelm, who's married to Carolina.
sentences.zh: 但并不是因为奥古斯特·威廉，他可是和卡罗琳结婚的人。

sentences.en: It's more because of Friedrich Schlegel, who used to be in love with Carolina, then gave her up for his brother.
sentences.zh: 更多是因为弗里德里希·施莱格尔，他曾经爱过卡罗琳，后来为了他兄弟放弃了她。

sentences.en: And then she just, you know, flounces off with the next one.
sentences.zh: 然后她就，你知道，跟下一个人跑了。

sentences.en: So that's the moment when he, I think, gets so pissed off that he's just, you know, all guards go down.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，就在那一刻，他气疯了，你知道，所有的防线都崩溃了。

sentences.en: And he and Dorothea just write so badly about Carolina, especially Dorothea, actually.
sentences.zh: 他和多萝西娅写了太多关于卡罗琳的坏话，尤其是多萝西娅，实际上。

sentences.en: Dorothea was, you know, she was, she was not very beautiful.
sentences.zh: 多萝西娅，你知道，她长得并不漂亮。

sentences.en: And she's the daughter of Moses Mendelssohn, right?
sentences.zh: 她是摩西·门德尔松的女儿，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the greatest German Enlightenment philosophers.
sentences.zh: 是的，德国启蒙运动最伟大的哲学家之一。

sentences.en: But she is, she feels always a little bit, I think, overshadowed by Carolina because everybody just adored her.
sentences.zh: 但她总是觉得，我想，被卡罗琳掩盖了光芒，因为每个人都崇拜她。

sentences.en: So the moment her lover turns against Carolina, Dorothea just writes an avalanche of horrible letters.
sentences.zh: 所以当她的爱人反过来对付卡罗琳时，多萝西娅就写了一连串可怕的信。

sentences.en: I mean, when you read them, you think that, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你读到这些信时，你会想，天哪。

sentences.en: And Carolina doesn't know that at the time.
sentences.zh: 而卡罗琳当时并不知道。

sentences.en: She lives together with her and, you know, perfectly nice and friendly to her.
sentences.zh: 她和她住在一起，你知道，表现得非常友善。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of backstabbing going on at the end.
sentences.zh: 所以最后有很多背后捅刀子的事情发生。

sentences.en: And there's one other, there's one other figure that we haven't mentioned again, I guess, a household name.
sentences.zh: 还有一个人，我们还没提到，我想，一个家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: And that is Hegel, the philosopher Hegel.
sentences.zh: 那就是黑格尔，哲学家黑格尔。

sentences.en: So he's not really part of the set, but he arrives towards the end, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他其实不是那个圈子的人，但他是在最后阶段才出现的，不是吗？

sentences.en: When I suppose they're, when they're in them, they're falling out phase and when the glory days are slightly paSt.
sentences.zh: 我想是在他们，在他们闹翻的阶段，当辉煌的日子稍微过去的时候。

sentences.en: So do you see Hegel?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为黑格尔算吗？

sentences.en: I mean, so in many ways that I suppose you could say the ancestor of Marx and of so many kind of modern ideas.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在很多方面，我想你可以说他是马克思和许多现代思想的鼻祖。

sentences.en: Do you see Hegel as part of this world as well?
sentences.zh: 你认为黑格尔也是这个世界的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Well, Hegel is basically, he comes in, as you said, quite towards the end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，黑格尔基本上，正如你所说，他是相当晚才出现的。

sentences.en: And it's like, you know, he's, he is, he's, I mean, now he's this kind of towering figure.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，他，他现在是一个泰斗级的人物。

sentences.en: But then he's very much, so he's, he had studied together with, with Schelling.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他非常，他曾和谢林一起学习。

sentences.en: And Schelling is the superstar.
sentences.zh: 而谢林是超级明星。

sentences.en: I mean, Schelling is made the youngest professor at the age of 23 in Jena.
sentences.zh: 我是说，谢林23岁就在耶拿被任命为最年轻的教授。

sentences.en: And when, when Hegel arrives, he, you know, it takes him like two or three years to make the decision to arrive.
sentences.zh: 当黑格尔到达时，他，你知道，他花了大概两三年才决定过来。

sentences.en: He's like, he ponders over everything.
sentences.zh: 他就像，他反复斟酌一切。

sentences.en: So as fast and restless as the others are, he's like very slow, kind of plodding along.
sentences.zh: 所以，和其他人一样快节奏和不安分相比，他非常缓慢，有点步履蹒跚。

sentences.en: And by the time he finally decides to come to Jena, the kind of whirlwind is kind of always blown out.
sentences.zh: 等他最终决定来到耶拿时，那种旋风般的势头已经消散了。

sentences.en: But he comes to Jena to be with Schelling because, you know, Schelling is the kind of superstar.
sentences.zh: 但他来到耶拿是为了和谢林在一起，因为，你知道，谢林是那种超级明星。

sentences.en: And then what happens is, as he, as he is in Jena, his, he moves away bit by bit from Schelling.
sentences.zh: 然后发生的事情是，当他在耶拿时，他一点一点地远离了谢林。

sentences.en: So Schelling leaves in 1803.
sentences.zh: 所以谢林在1803年离开了。

sentences.en: And after that, Hegel really begins his own journey.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，黑格尔才真正开始了属于他自己的旅程。

sentences.en: And he turns against, in his philosophy, he really turns against all this kind of craziness and kind of the philosophy, which, which loves art and imagination.
sentences.zh: 在他的哲学中，他真正反对所有这些疯狂的东西，以及那种热爱艺术和想象力的哲学。

sentences.en: And he says like, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，不，不。

sentences.en: And he hates nature, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他讨厌自然，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, he goes, he goes to Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，他去了瑞士。

sentences.en: And everybody's like in all of the Alps.
sentences.zh: 每个人都对阿尔卑斯山赞叹不已。

sentences.en: And he's like more interested in the technique of Swiss cheese making.
sentences.zh: 而他却对瑞士奶酪的制作工艺更感兴趣。

sentences.en: But what he says, he basically says, hold on, philosophy is a serious business.
sentences.zh: 但他所说的是，他基本上说，等一下，哲学是一项严肃的事业。

sentences.en: So let's strip all that kind of art and imagination out of it again.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们把那些艺术和想象力从哲学中剔除出去。

sentences.en: So he is, he kind of ends it really.
sentences.zh: 所以他，他确实终结了那个时代。

sentences.en: And there's this amazing scene, you know, where you sometimes think, you know, facts are just so much better than fiction.
sentences.zh: 有一个惊人的场景，你知道，有时你会想，事实比虚构更离奇。

sentences.en: You couldn't invent it.
sentences.zh: 你根本编不出这样的故事。

sentences.en: So there's the Battle of Jena when Napoleon arrives with his 150,000 French soldiers and they descend onto Jena and they destroy the kind of almighty Prussian army.
sentences.zh: 那是耶拿战役，拿破仑带着他15万法军士兵抵达，他们降临耶拿，摧毁了那支不可一世的普鲁士军队。

sentences.en: And on the day and the day before the battle, you have Hegel with the manuscript of the phenomenon, I can never get this word out, the phenomenology of spirit.
sentences.zh: 就在战役前一天，黑格尔带着《精神现象学》的手稿——我永远念不好这个词——

sentences.en: It's his only copy and he puts it on the stagecoat out of Jena.
sentences.zh: 那是他唯一的副本，他把它放在了离开耶拿的驿站马车上。

sentences.en: And then he sees Napoleon on a horse and calls him the world soul.
sentences.zh: 然后他看到拿破仑骑在马上，称他为“世界灵魂”。

sentences.en: So it's this extraordinary moment, which is really, that's the end of Jena.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非凡的时刻，这确实是耶拿时代的终结。

sentences.en: Because after the battle, Jena has completely destroyed, the students all left, leave and so, but Hegel is there at the very last moment, like handing over his manuscript.
sentences.zh: 因为战役之后，耶拿被彻底摧毁，学生们都离开了，但黑格尔在最后一刻还在那里，就像在递交他的手稿。

sentences.en: So it's almost like a sort of harbinger of the herald of the 19th century at the end of the 18th, I guess, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他几乎像是18世纪末19世纪初的先驱，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, sort of pointing ahead to the great ideologies that will dominate, you know, the future.
sentences.zh: 我是说，某种程度上指向了未来将主导世界的伟大意识形态。

sentences.en: It's an amazing moment, actually, because Napoleon himself is a figure like that, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个惊人的时刻，因为拿破仑本人就是那样的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Napoleon himself is a sort of enlightenment figure who is anticipating.
sentences.zh: 所以拿破仑本人是一个预示着未来的启蒙运动人物。

sentences.en: But also a romantic figure.
sentences.zh: 但也是一个浪漫主义人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's anticipating the dictators and the, you know, the monstrous ambitions of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，但他预示着20世纪的独裁者和那些可怕的野心。

sentences.en: But Hegel sees him as, you know, this is basically where this progression from like feudal system to democracies and freedom.
sentences.zh: 但黑格尔视他为，你知道，这基本上就是从封建制度向民主和自由进步的过程。

sentences.en: He's basically the end of history for Hegel.
sentences.zh: 对黑格尔来说，他基本上就是历史的终结。

sentences.en: When he sees him, he, you know, that because we think, oh, the French are, you know, in Jena and the Germans don't really want this.
sentences.zh: 当他看到他时，他，你知道，因为我们认为，哦，法国人在耶拿，德国人并不真正想要这个。

sentences.en: But there are quite a lot of Germans who want the French to come because they want to be liberated.
sentences.zh: 但确实有很多德国人希望法国人来，因为他们想要获得解放。

sentences.en: They want to live in a republic and not in, you know, in absolutism.
sentences.zh: 他们想生活在共和国里，而不是生活在专制统治下。

sentences.en: So Hegel, although his life is threatened, he wants the French to win.
sentences.zh: 所以黑格尔，尽管他的生命受到威胁，但他还是希望法国人获胜。

sentences.en: But Andrea, so the Jena set basically ends with that they all have bust ups, they all run off and marry with one another and end up hating each other.
sentences.zh: 但是安德烈，耶拿圈子基本上就是这样结束的：他们都闹翻了，都跑了，互相结婚，最后互相憎恨。

sentences.en: And then Napoleon comes up and basically kind of trashes the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 然后拿破仑来了，基本上把一切都摧毁了。

sentences.en: But one other thing that I picked up from the book is that a lot of these figures end up veering quite sharply to the right.
sentences.zh: 但我从书中发现的另一件事是，许多这样的人物最终都急剧转向右翼。

sentences.en: So they tend to become Catholic, they tend to become quite politically reactionary.
sentences.zh: 所以他们倾向于皈依天主教，倾向于变得非常政治反动。

sentences.en: And do you think that that kind of parabola of kind of burning radicalism fading out, veering back into reaction?
sentences.zh: 你认为那种激进主义燃烧殆尽、转向反动的抛物线，

sentences.en: Do you think that that is that setting a kind of prototype that will be followed through the 19th, 20th century?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是否设定了一种将在19、20世纪被遵循的原型？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think it is something that happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种经常发生的事情。

sentences.en: Like the big revolutionaries often become, you know, dictators and, you know, nationalistic and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 就像伟大的革命者往往会变成独裁者、民族主义者之类的。

sentences.en: So I don't know if they're the prototype.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道他们是否是原型。

sentences.en: I think it's maybe it's in human nature.
sentences.zh: 我想这也许是人性使然。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe, maybe, maybe.
sentences.zh: 是的，也许，也许。

sentences.en: I fear.
sentences.zh: 我担心是这样。

sentences.en: Just to sum, give us a sense of just how significant this is, because we've about half the podcast has been on the philosophy,
sentences.zh: 总结一下，让我们感受一下这有多重要，因为我们播客的一半时间都在谈论哲学，

sentences.en: but the other half, I'm afraid it's entirely my fault, has been all about the.
sentences.zh: 但另一半，恐怕全怪我，都在谈论这些。

sentences.en: You can see where Tom's interests lie, Andrea.
sentences.zh: 安德烈，你可以看出汤姆的兴趣所在。

sentences.en: So just for people, listeners who may not be absolutely au fait with idealist philosophy,
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些可能不太熟悉唯心主义哲学的听众，

sentences.en: just give us a sense of how important this is, not just for philosophy, but for the whole sweep of European history.
sentences.zh: 请让我们感受一下这不仅对哲学，而且对整个欧洲历史进程的重要性。

sentences.en: I think basically they changed our world.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们基本上改变了我们的世界。

sentences.en: It's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: They put the self at centre stage and it has stayed there for the better of the worst forever.
sentences.zh: 他们把“自我”置于中心舞台，无论好坏，它就一直留在那里。

sentences.en: And we have, from the moment they put the self at the centre, we had, or people had to deal with the, with the perils of this kind of newly emboldened ich or self.
sentences.zh: 从他们把“自我”置于中心的那一刻起，我们就不得不面对这种新赋予权力的“自我”所带来的危险。

sentences.en: And it is, it is the same kind of tiptoeing we still have to do today.
sentences.zh: 这和我们今天依然需要小心翼翼处理的问题是一样的。

sentences.en: And, and I think it is, it has made us who we are.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为这造就了今天的我们。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, it starts with the enlightenment, but this is the moment where, this is why we are a selfish society today, full stop.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这始于启蒙运动，但这就是为什么我们今天是一个自私社会的时刻，句号。

sentences.en: I think that's as simple as that.

sentences.en: we have for long thought that we are free to think, to form our opinions, to control our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们长期以来一直认为我们有自由去思考、去形成我们的观点、去掌控我们的生活。

sentences.en: But right now, all of that, this very core of our society is very much under threat, be it through Russia's cyber interference in democratic elections, be it through the,

sentences.en: Our, you know, our democracies are hollowed out right now through liars and through despots.
sentences.zh: 我们的民主正被骗子和暴君掏空。

sentences.en: So I think right now it's such an important moment to remind ourselves why, you know, when did we become free?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为现在是一个非常重要的时刻，提醒我们自己，你知道，我们是什么时候变得自由的？

sentences.en: Where does this hard one self-determination came from?
sentences.zh: 这种来之不易的自我决定权从何而来？

sentences.en: So in a way the Jena set has given, you know, has given us, we, our mind wings, but how we use them, that's entirely up for us.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，耶拿圈子给了我们思想的翅膀，但我们如何使用它们，完全取决于我们自己。

sentences.en: And I'm interested in history.
sentences.zh: 我对历史很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And I mean, you will probably definitely agree with me.
sentences.zh: 而且，我想你大概一定会同意我的观点。

sentences.en: It's not like a dusty old pile of ideas.
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么陈旧过时的想法堆砌。

sentences.en: It's, you know, I'm interested in history because I want to know why we are who we are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我之所以对历史感兴趣，是因为我想知道我们为什么会成为现在的我们。

sentences.en: So with my Humboldt book, for example, I looked at the relationship between humankind and nature to understand why we're destroying our planet.
sentences.zh: 比如在写《洪堡》那本书时，我研究了人类与自然之间的关系，以理解我们为何正在破坏自己的星球。

sentences.en: And with this book, I really wanted to know now, why are we such a selfish society?
sentences.zh: 而写这本书时，我真的很想知道，为什么我们现在会变成一个如此自私的社会？

sentences.zh: 但同时，我也想提醒自己，你知道，在耶拿派的语境里，“自私”其实是一个褒义词。
